thread.title: Apple is curbing sex, violence and profanity in TV shows

title: Apple is curbing sex, violence and profanity in TV shows
text:
Photo: Spencer Platt / Getty Images Apple is curbing sex, violence and profanity in TV shows The digital platform will look more like NBC than HBO. Author: Denver Business Journal Published: 3:30 PM Updated: 3:30 PM
DENVER BUSINESS JOURNAL — Apple Inc.’s forthcoming digital video platform will look more like NBC than HBO, as CEO Tim Cook has ixnayed sex, violence and profanity in content developed for the computer giant.
Cook pulled the plug on “Vital Signs,” a semi-autobiographical drama based on the life of hip-hop mogul Dr. Dre, because it included scenes of drug use, an orgy and drawn guns, reported The Wall Street Journal.
The mandate for more family-friendly fare has resulted in Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) pulling away from some projects while adjusting the tone on others: The company discussed but ultimately decided not to pursue projects with Keanu Reeves appearing as a hit man, Michael Fassbender as a rally-car driver, and Whitney Cummings in a #MeToo pitch set in a college.
Meanwhile, the company replaced the showrunners on “Amazing Stories” and a drama about a morning news show starring Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon in order to tweak the shows’ respective tones, and Apple greenlit a series from M. Night Shyamalan about a couple who lose a young child, provided the script does away with crucifixes on the walls of their house.
